build.prompt_version: Trump Diary Phase 1 Discovery Prompt v1

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration and citizenship as instruments of domestic control and tiered belonging
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern of using immigration enforcement, detention, status review, and citizenship threats not merely for border administration but as tools to discipline communities, punish critics, sort populations by favored status, and normalize a tiered legal order.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration System Turned Into an Authoritarian Testbed
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly frames immigration law, deportation, detention, and judge purges as a proving ground for punitive politicized governance.

supporting_developments.development_title: Chicago as a Laboratory for Militarized Immigration Crackdowns and Protest Suppression
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows city-level application of immigration raids and detention as coercive governance against an opposition-led jurisdiction.

supporting_developments.development_title: Militarized immigration crackdowns turn Chicago and Portland into test beds for domestic force
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Links immigration enforcement to troop deployment and federal coercion in cities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and detention systems are hardened while oversight and due process are stripped away
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly captures deportation escalation, court purges, detention expansion, and erosion of safeguards.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and security powers weaponized against dissenters and noncitizens
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows immigration and security authorities being used against both migrants and political critics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and security apparatus repurposed for domestic control and political targeting
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Makes the domestic-control logic explicit, including detention, visa revocations, and selective refugee priorities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a militarized, privatized detention regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows raids, detention expansion, privatization, and family trauma as recurring features of the same control system.

supporting_developments.development_title: Stratified citizenship and coercive social policy: from passports and homelessness to tribal climate aid
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread from immigration to broader stratified citizenship and selective deprivation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement escalates into a rights crisis, met by scattered judicial pushback
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the pattern of abusive raids, biometric tracking, extraterritorial detention, and partial court limits.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and foreign policy tools used to punish dissent and project hard power abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows immigration status and removal being used against disfavored speakers and critics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Operation Charlotte’s Web and National Guard deployments turn immigration enforcement into a domestic security campaign
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Illustrates interior raids and Guard deployments as a domestic security strategy built around immigration enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship become central tools of social control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Most direct articulation of status review, de-naturalization threats, and enforcement against families and long-term residents.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and quasi-paramilitary tactics are turned inward to intimidate communities and lawmakers
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows masked raids and immigration-linked intimidation as part of domestic coercion.

supporting_developments.development_title: From rhetoric to regime: a racialized immigration crackdown and tiered citizenship
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures the mature form of the thread: racialized rhetoric, asylum freezes, travel bans, status reviews, and raids.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest and dissent squeezed by immigration crackdowns, policing tactics, and targeted investigations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows immigration tools being deployed against protest spaces and civic resistance.

aliases: immigration and detention as domestic control
immigration and security powers weaponized against dissenters
immigration and citizenship as tools of social control
inclusion_notes: Include deportation, detention, status review, visa revocation, asylum restrictions, de-naturalization threats, and judge/court changes when they function as tools of control rather than routine policy.
Include cases where immigration powers are used against critics, opposition-led cities, protesters, or mixed-status communities.
Include selective refugee or citizenship preferences when they create a hierarchy of belonging.
exclusion_notes: Exclude purely foreign-policy migration diplomacy unless it clearly feeds back into domestic coercion.
Exclude general militarization unless immigration enforcement is a central mechanism.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_SECURITY_FORCES_AGAINST_DISSENT, which centers protest policing and emergency-force logic more broadly.
Distinct from cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY, which centers prosecutions, pardons, and justice-system favoritism.
Overlaps with cand_STRATIFIED_RIGHTS_AND_IDENTITY_TARGETING where immigration hierarchy broadens into general tiered citizenship.
merge_suggestions: May merge later with similar labels like 'immigration as authoritarian testbed' or 'immigration as domestic control'.
Keep separate from broader protest/militarization thread unless later windows erase the distinction.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Law, prosecution, pardons, and courts bent toward retaliation for opponents and protection for allies
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which DOJ, FBI, prosecutorial authority, clemency, secrecy, and legal narratives are used to punish critics, reopen grievances, shield connected insiders, and blur the rule of law into partisan or personal rule.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and Courts Bent Toward Retaliation and Elite Protection
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly identifies politicized prosecutions, selective shielding, and partial judicial resistance.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOJ and FBI are repurposed into tools of political retribution and protection
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the justice system protecting allies and targeting critics through staffing, secrecy, and prosecutorial choices.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates direct attacks on political opponents, media, and protest as "terrorism"
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects rhetorical targeting of opponents to legal and security mechanisms.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and clemency become tools for rewarding allies and punishing perceived enemies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers pardons, commutations, selective prosecutions, and DOJ self-dealing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and courts increasingly weaponized against critics as Trump seeks personal legal revenge
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Most explicit articulation of legal revenge, politicized prosecution, and relitigation of grievances.

supporting_developments.development_title: Pardons, politicized justice, and the burial of elite wrongdoing
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines clemency, selective inquiry, secrecy, and lawfare against opponents into one clear pattern.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and justice bent toward Trump’s interests: pardons, politicized probes, and elite impunity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same pattern through pardons, investigations, captured regulators, and elite favoritism.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law as weapon: Epstein files, targeted investigations, and elite impunity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows transparency fights, targeted probes, secrecy tactics, misconduct, and elite-friendly justice in the same thread.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates use of law and security apparatus against political opponents
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Illustrates investigations of lawmakers alongside pardons for pro-Trump election offenders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts deliver mixed signals as some rulings check abuse while others entrench conservative power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides contextual evidence on the judiciary’s uneven role within the lawfare environment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and clemency repurposed to shield corrupt elites and rewrite legal continuity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through mass pardons, appointment abuse, and attacks on legal continuity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil and criminal accountability for past abuses advances unevenly through the Epstein files and January 6 cases
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the countervailing struggle for accountability within a broader environment of impunity.

aliases: pardons for allies, punishment for enemies
inclusion_notes: Include politicized prosecutions, selective non-prosecution, pardons/commutations for allies, secrecy used to shield insiders, and DOJ/FBI staffing changes that alter legal neutrality.
Include judicial conduct or court interventions when they are part of a wider struggle over weaponized law or impunity.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general court resistance unless it directly bears on retaliatory prosecution, impunity, or capture of legal institutions.
Exclude election-rule manipulation unless the legal weaponization itself is central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ELECTION_RULE_MANIPULATION, which centers representation and electoral rules rather than prosecutorial power.
Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE, which focuses more on bureaucracy and regulatory institutions than justice institutions.
Often overlaps with Epstein transparency fights; those can be treated as a subcase of this thread or of information control depending on emphasis.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels such as 'rule by law', 'justice system politicization', or 'retaliation and elite protection'.
Keep broad enough to include pardons, investigations, and secrecy around elite misconduct.
split_suggestions: If later windows support it, a sub-thread on 'clemency and impunity for allies' could split from broader DOJ weaponization.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information control, propaganda, record erasure, and narrative management
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern of curating what the public can know through propaganda, AI content, press restrictions, deletion or manipulation of records and data, pressure on media and universities, and symbolic control over public memory.

supporting_developments.development_title: Coordinated Information Warfare: Deepfakes, Pseudoscience, and Platform Pressure
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces official disinformation, AI manipulation, pseudoscience, platform pressure, and suppression of independent voices.

supporting_developments.development_title: Culture, Education, and History Rewritten to Legitimize State Power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into curated historical memory and educational pressure.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, disinformation, and symbolic politics consolidate Trump’s narrative dominance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly links press access control, disinformation, and leader-centric symbolic politics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Press freedom and academic independence squeezed by gag rules, lawsuits, and funding threats
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows institutional pressure on press and universities as part of narrative control.

supporting_developments.development_title: National story and public space remade around nationalist and anti–welfare state symbols
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Demonstrates public-memory engineering through symbols, monuments, and rhetoric.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump repurposes the White House and federal records for personal glorification and secrecy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights record suppression and symbolic refashioning of civic space.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, AI propaganda, and a curated media ecosystem reshape public perception
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces propaganda, selective media access, and degradation of the information environment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and civic memory reshaped through propaganda, censorship, and chaos
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Most explicit statement of propaganda, censorship, and chaos as a governing method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Knowledge and culture under pressure: universities, media, and identity narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows ideological pressure on universities and media plus narrative framing around identity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information warfare and AI‑driven disinformation reshape elections and protest narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds AI-driven distortion in campaigns, media intimidation, and speculative misinformation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Struggle over Epstein files and elite accountability collides with efforts to curate public memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects secrecy around elite wrongdoing to curated national memory and museum content.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information and memory are curated by power—from trans erasure to media pressure and Chinese controls
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures data erasure, media pressure, and curation of memory in explicit thread form.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, media, and memory are aggressively curated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows suppression of economic data, science manipulation, media threats, and cultural-memory control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Culture-war governance targets schools, libraries, and universities
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides institutional examples of educational and cultural narrative policing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information warfare, managed opacity, and the curation of memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the same pattern through hostile media targeting, hidden data, politicized science, and selective transparency.

inclusion_notes: Include AI propaganda, media intimidation, platform pressure, deletion or rewriting of public information, suppression of data, and pressure on universities, museums, or schools to conform ideologically.
Include symbolic politics and memory curation when used to shape public understanding and legitimize power.
exclusion_notes: Exclude ordinary partisan messaging unless tied to institutional control of information channels.
Exclude legal secrecy that is better understood as part of justice-system impunity unless public-information control is central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY, though secrecy over Epstein or prosecutions can overlap.
Distinct from cand_STRATIFIED_RIGHTS_AND_IDENTITY_TARGETING, though erasure of trans identity is both an information-control and rights hierarchy issue.
Potential super-thread candidate with sub-threads for press/university pressure and public-memory rewriting, but window evidence supports keeping one strong thread.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels like 'public-record erasure', 'propaganda state', or 'memory control'.
Preserve breadth: this thread clearly includes both media/information channels and symbolic-memory curation.
split_suggestions: Could later split into 'information warfare/press control' and 'memory/history/education control' if cross-window evidence warrants.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Administrative state capture through civil-service purge, agency politicization, and regulatory redirection
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern of hollowing out neutral administrative capacity, politicizing hiring and oversight, capturing regulatory agencies, and redirecting bureaucratic machinery toward loyalists, donors, or ideological allies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown and Budget Crisis Used to Purge Civil Service and Punish Blue Jurisdictions
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows shutdown leverage being used to force resignations, layoffs, and partisan resource allocation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil Service and Oversight Structures Politicized and Hollowed Out
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Direct statement of mass resignations, loyalty staffing, oversight-office overhaul, and bureaucratic intimidation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown becomes a weapon to punish opponents and weaken the federal workforce
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds workforce weakening and governance by shutdown leverage.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service and watchdogs purged as Trump tightens personal control over the state
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows hiring centralization, IG firings, layoffs, and policy-office gutting as state capture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service and regulatory agencies are purged, captured, and used as political leverage
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly anchors the thread in regulatory capture, purge task forces, layoffs, and shutdown leverage.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown weaponized to attack SNAP, hollow out CDC, and sideline Congress
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows agency hollowing and use of shutdown conditions to restructure public-health capacity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Opposition constrained and civil service politicized through procedural and personnel control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly names civil-service politicization, threats to workers, and centralized personnel control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Administrative state capture: CFPB, FHFA, USDA, and EPA repurposed for partisan and corporate aims
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Best explicit articulation of the thread at agency level across multiple departments.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security and civil service institutions bent toward loyalty, patronage, and private contractors
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows loyalty perks, patronage contracting, outsourcing, and weakening of institutional norms.

inclusion_notes: Include mass firings, loyalty-based staffing, attacks on inspectors general, personnel centralization, regulatory capture, and agency redirection toward partisan or corporate ends.
Include outsourcing and contractor favoritism when it weakens neutral state capacity.
exclusion_notes: Exclude justice-system weaponization unless the emphasis is agency staffing/capture rather than prosecutions or pardons.
Exclude shutdown harm alone unless it is used to restructure or politicize administration.
boundary_notes: Closely related to cand_SHUTDOWN_AND_FISCAL_WEAPONIZATION but broader: this thread is about remaking the bureaucracy itself.
Distinct from cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY, though DOJ/FBI politicization can sit at the border.
May also overlap with crony-capitalist regulatory favoritism, but the administrative machinery remains the center of gravity.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels such as 'civil service hollowing' or 'bureaucratic capture'.
Keep separate from shutdown thread because the personnel/oversight pattern persists beyond the shutdown itself.
split_suggestions: A later sub-thread on 'watchdog and inspector-general purge' may be useful if repeated independently.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Shutdown and budget authority weaponized to coerce workers, starve programs, and punish opponents
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which shutdown conditions, appropriations paralysis, funding freezes, selective back pay, and social-program withholding are used as instruments of partisan leverage, institutional weakening, and unequal punishment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown and Budget Crisis Used to Purge Civil Service and Punish Blue Jurisdictions
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces shutdown governance as a weapon against workers, agencies, and disfavored jurisdictions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown becomes a weapon to punish opponents and weaken the federal workforce
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly frames the shutdown as leverage for restructuring programs and harming workers.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown hardball turns Congress into theater while Trump seizes budget power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows appropriations paralysis being exploited to centralize budget power and selectively freeze funds.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown weaponized to attack SNAP, hollow out CDC, and sideline Congress
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Pushes the thread into social-program deprivation and agency restructuring during prolonged shutdown.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown weaponized: SNAP defiance, court clashes, and economic fallout
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Demonstrates court defiance, hardship, and economic damage flowing from shutdown leverage.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown ends on Trump’s terms while Congress stages limited oversight theater
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the culmination of the shutdown weaponization strategy and its institutional consequences.

inclusion_notes: Include withholding of benefits, selective freezes, appropriations bypasses, threats to workers, and congressional paralysis when used as leverage.
Include shutdown-era attacks on social programs and workforce protections.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general administrative capture unless shutdown or budget leverage is the operative mechanism.
Exclude broader economic cronyism absent fiscal hostage-taking or appropriations coercion.
boundary_notes: Narrower than cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE: this thread centers the shutdown/fiscal lever specifically.
Related to cand_CRONY_CAPITALISM_AND_PRIVATE_STATE_FUSION where funds are redirected to allies, but the key logic here is coercive budget governance.
merge_suggestions: May merge with labels like 'budget power seizure' or 'shutdown governance as weapon'.
Worth preserving separately because the shutdown is a distinct governing method visible across multiple consecutive weeks.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Militarization of domestic politics and use of security forces against dissent
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern of framing protest, opposition-led cities, and domestic critics as security threats, then using troops, Guard deployments, emergency rhetoric, raids, riot control, or war-on-enemies language to justify coercive force inside normal civic space.

supporting_developments.development_title: Militarization of Domestic Politics and the War Framing of Dissent
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes the war framing of domestic opponents and threatened troop use in cities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Chicago as a Laboratory for Militarized Immigration Crackdowns and Protest Suppression
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows concrete city-level blending of raids, crowd control, and intimidation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Militarized immigration crackdowns turn Chicago and Portland into test beds for domestic force
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers Guard deployments and militarized federal force in opposition-governed cities.

supporting_developments.development_title: White House flirts with Insurrection Act logic and new war powers to justify lethal force
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides the legal and rhetorical architecture for domestic use of force.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates direct attacks on political opponents, media, and protest as "terrorism"
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows dissent being rhetorically recoded as terrorism to enable coercive response.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest and opposition recast as terrorism ahead of "No Kings" rallies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly ties terrorism framing to impending protests and militarized responses.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and emergency powers are turned inward against dissent and immigrants
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows Guard deployment, Insurrection Act talk, and ICE force directed inward.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and foreign policy tools used to punish dissent and project hard power abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Keeps the dissent-punishment frame alive across security tools and military posture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Operation Charlotte’s Web and National Guard deployments turn immigration enforcement into a domestic security campaign
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows domestic deployment of military-style force under immigration pretexts.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and quasi-paramilitary tactics are turned inward to intimidate communities and lawmakers
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Strongly captures internal intimidation through masked operations, raids, and coercive spectacle.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and war powers stretched toward extrajudicial violence and regime protection
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread from domestic militarization into politically bent security institutions and force.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest and dissent squeezed by immigration crackdowns, policing tactics, and targeted investigations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows protest suppression as a continuing governing method across policing and investigation.

inclusion_notes: Include Guard or troop deployments, Insurrection Act talk, terrorism framing of protest, riot-control tactics, and militarized raids in civic spaces.
Include immigration raids when the key point is their use as domestic intimidation or protest suppression rather than immigration hierarchy itself.
exclusion_notes: Exclude foreign war powers unless directly linked back to domestic force logic or security normalization.
Exclude general immigration enforcement unless dissent suppression or militarized civic-space control is central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_DOMESTIC_CONTROL, though many developments sit at the border between the two.
Distinct from cand_EXECUTIVE_WAR_POWERS_AND_MILITARY_POLITICIZATION, which centers unilateral military authority in broader strategic terms, not just domestic dissent.
Can absorb local 'test bed' cases like Chicago or Charlotte as concrete manifestations rather than separate threads.
merge_suggestions: May merge with labels such as 'militarized repression' or 'protest criminalization and domestic force'.
Keep distinct from broader war-powers thread if later windows continue to show separate domestic applications.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Crony capitalism and private-state fusion in economic and foreign policy

supporting_developments.development_title: Trade, tariffs, and corporate deals are personalized into instruments of presidential power

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and foreign policy intertwine with elite enrichment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows bailouts, Gulf deals, stablecoin ties, and insider benefits linked to state policy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and foreign economic policy intertwine with family and donor enrichment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through tariffs, bailouts, contracts, and energy favoritism benefiting family and allies.

supporting_developments.development_title: White House flirts with Insurrection Act logic and new war powers to justify lethal force

notes_on_window: Window 37-46 shows especially strong continuity around immigration as domestic control, weaponized law/impunity, information control, and administrative-state capture.
The shutdown is clearly a major recurring method in weeks 37-43, then recedes; it is best kept as a distinct window-visible thread rather than stretched beyond its evidence.
Several developments show strong overlap between immigration control and domestic militarization; boundary notes preserve the distinction between status-based hierarchy and force-based repression.
Anti-trans and broader identity-targeting become especially visible later in the window and may be emergent rather than fully sustained in this slice alone.
Cronyism/private-state fusion is visible across economic, foreign-policy, and pardon/contract stories, suggesting a durable cross-domain pattern.
